1970.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1970-71 ed. (M-57), Table 43 (p. 100, rates at December 31, 1970): City of Louisville 1.25%, Jefferson County 1.75%, with footnote 2 that a taxpayer subject to the city's 1.25% may credit it against the county's 1.75%, so a city resident pays 1.75% in all. The 0.2% transit tax (Mass Transportation Program approved by the electorate November 5, 1974) did not yet exist; Components as later recorded (city, transit, school board) not itemized in the table.

1971.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1972 ed. (M-74), Table 99 (p. 226, rates at December 31, 1971): City of Louisville 1.25%, Jefferson County 1.75%, with footnote 2 that a taxpayer subject to the city's 1.25% may credit it against the county's 1.75%, so a city resident pays 1.75% in all. Components as later recorded (city, transit, school board) not itemized in the table.

1973.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1973-74 ed. (M-79), Table 150 (p. 292, rates at July 1, 1973): City of Louisville 1.25%, Jefferson County 2.0%, with footnote 2 that a taxpayer subject to the city's 1.25% may credit it against the county's 2.0%, so a city resident pays 2.0% in all. The 2.2% of the 1976-77 edition includes the 0.2% transit tax approved by the electorate November 5, 1974, so 1972 and 1974-1975 are not recorded. Components as later recorded (city, transit, school board) not itemized in the table.

1976.notes: ACIR Significant Features of Fiscal Federalism 1976-77 ed. vol. II, Table 116 (rates as of July 1, 1976): City of Louisville 1.45%, Jefferson County 2.2%, with the footnote that a taxpayer subject to the city's 1.45% may credit it against the county's 2.2%, so a city resident pays 2.2% in all (1.45% to the city plus the uncredited 0.75% of the county levy). Components as later recorded (1.25% city, 0.2% transit, 0.75% school board) not itemized in the table.
